question: Can verified span credit rank the right interventions when its absolute cross-history kernel effect is too small? Redistribute the native third-slot activity budget by rank and directly maximize physically paired return on nested held-history donor scores. Compare to using exactly the same return and optimizer without extra selection credit. The fixed two source skills, common slots, native actor, writers, reader and K=3 stay fixed.
inputs: Use the joint-mask fit followed separately by joint-repaired, after applying every previously measured writer-block veto per original question before the capped-source intervention. Both contain the same 60 background-weighted decisions from 12 initial factorial and 12 randomized donor windows on six training dialogues. Return and verified signed selection labels come only from these donors. Compare raw plus verified credit, raw alone, and raw plus cyclically permuted credit within each history, stage and observation weight. Only actual pre-write controller state and native logits are available at deployment.
fit: Separate root and terminal. For target H, exclude H. For each calibration donor D, predict its three scores from other histories excluding both H and D, using the published positive-cosine-power-eight kernel, its constant one prior mass, and equal weight per training history. Learn the allocation by optimizing the original (mask- or repair-adjusted) paired return alone for all three orderings. Give calibration histories equal mass and keep within-history observation weights. A threshold selects the upper or lower native log-odds bound (+2 or -2) and all-equal scores share their threshold decision. Enumerate thresholds splitting distinct observed scores at their midpoint, including both constant decisions. Maximize paired gain over mixtures of two thresholds, subject to retaining the weighted native activity rate at each stage. This represents the optimum over mixtures of arbitrary monotone thresholds under one budget. Never take training gain below native. Ties prefer the smallest probability movement and then deterministic threshold order. Refit the kernel excluding H alone before application; all threshold rules and weights freeze before reading evaluation outcomes. Test-set labels do not set budgets.
diagnostics: Compare native, terminal, soft uncalibrated credit kernel, return-only allocation, and shuffled-credit allocation. On the 88 already measured calibration questions compute label-informed diagnostic ceilings under a common threshold mapping per stage, separately using the held-history raw or verified-credit score ordering, and using actual paired delta as an omniscient ordering. All diagnostic ceilings have the same question-weighted native use per stage. They do not train policies or enter a cross-dialogue claim. Measure how much of the original kernel attenuation is explained by similarity mass, signed cancellation, and native probability saturation.
evaluation: Record calibration outcomes separately. Freeze each stage before scoring later windows and separate any window with either path already scored. For all 40 randomized later windows / 378 questions compute actual focal paired expected F1, joint Horvitz-Thompson estimates, per-dialogue and per-type F1, dialogue-cluster intervals, changed probabilities and token budgets. Include a constant log-odds offset per pivot matching the candidate's question-weighted realized use, fitted without returns. Require full later coverage, >=.02 F1 over both native and terminal with positive HT effects, positive vs raw, shuffled, soft and matched-rate, >=4/6 histories better than matched-rate and positive strict prospective gain against native and return-only before independent development and full locked LoCoMo/LongMemEval-S evaluation.
